stem: Which statement best captures the value of the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform?
opts: It unifies data engineering, SQL analytics, BI, and AI on a governed lakehouse
It is purely a dashboarding tool that connects to external warehouses
It is a standalone relational database engine for OLTP workloads
It is a file storage service with no built-in compute
expl: The Data Intelligence Platform unifies engineering, SQL analytics, BI, and AI over a governed lakehouse (Delta Lake + Unity Catalog), with embedded AI to assist tasks like writing queries.

stem: What is the correct Unity Catalog object hierarchy, from top to bottom?
expl: The UC namespace is Metastore (one per region) -> Catalog -> Schema (database) -> objects such as Table, View, Volume, and Function.

stem: In Databricks SQL, which compute resource runs an analyst's queries and dashboards?
expl: SQL warehouses are the compute optimized for SQL and BI workloads in Databricks SQL, with autoscaling and concurrency for interactive queries and dashboards.

stem: An analyst wants the warehouse that starts in seconds and requires no infrastructure setup. Which should they choose?
expl: Serverless SQL warehouses are fully managed by Databricks with near-instant startup and automatic scaling, minimizing the analyst's wait time and operational overhead.

stem: What does Photon provide for Databricks SQL queries?
opts: A vectorized engine that speeds up SQL queries
A proprietary storage format for tables
A data sharing protocol for external partners
A Git integration for versioning notebooks
expl: Photon is the native, vectorized (C++) execution engine that accelerates SQL and DataFrame workloads, improving performance and cost efficiency.

stem: What is the default table format in the Databricks lakehouse that adds ACID transactions over object storage?
expl: Delta Lake is the default table format, adding ACID, time travel, and schema enforcement/evolution on top of files in object storage.

stem: An analyst needs to see which source table a gold column was derived from, without reading code. Which Unity Catalog feature helps?
expl: Unity Catalog data lineage automatically tracks the flow of data between tables and columns (upstream/downstream), revealing where a value comes from.

stem: What is the Databricks Marketplace?
opts: A scheduler for recurring ETL jobs
An open exchange for third-party datasets
expl: The Marketplace is an open exchange where providers publish data, models, and solutions; consumption uses Delta Sharing, so no manual data replication is required.

stem: Which interface lets an analyst visually browse catalogs, schemas, tables, permissions, and lineage?
expl: Catalog Explorer is the UI for browsing and inspecting Unity Catalog objects: catalogs, schemas, tables, columns, comments, tags, permissions, and lineage.

stem: What does it mean that the lakehouse separates compute from storage?
opts: Compute and storage are the same physical resource
Data lives only in warehouse memory during a session
Cheap object storage with on-demand compute
Storage is always local to the SQL warehouse
expl: The architecture keeps storage (data in open object storage) separate from compute (ephemeral, scalable warehouses/clusters), so each can scale and be paid for independently.

stem: Which statement about Unity Catalog as a governance layer is correct?
opts: It is a query execution engine
Unified governance for data and AI
It is a columnar file format
expl: Unity Catalog is the unified governance layer (access control, lineage, auditing, discovery) for data and AI assets, shareable across workspaces in the same account/region.

stem: Which best describes the lakehouse architecture?
opts: It requires moving data into a closed warehouse before analysis
It supports only BI workloads, never ML
Data-lake flexibility plus warehouse structure and governance
It replaces object storage with a proprietary relational database
expl: The lakehouse unifies both worlds: open, cheap object storage (lake) plus ACID, governance, and performance (warehouse) via Delta Lake + Unity Catalog, serving BI, ETL, and ML on one copy.

stem: Using the three-level namespace, how does an analyst reference table clients in schema sales of catalog prod?
expl: The three-level namespace is catalog.schema.table, so it is prod.sales.clients.

stem: Which SQL warehouse type generally has the fastest startup and least management overhead?
expl: The serverless warehouse starts in seconds and is fully managed by Databricks; classic warehouses run in the customer's cloud and typically have slower startup.

stem: An analyst wants to know which tables are trusted and approved for analysis. Which Unity Catalog capability signals this?
expl: Unity Catalog lets owners certify assets and apply tags, helping analysts identify trustworthy, approved data for analyses and dashboards.
src: Docs: UC certified data and tags

stem: What is a benefit of storing data in open formats (Delta/Parquet) in the lakehouse?
opts: It prevents the use of SQL
It makes the data unreadable outside Databricks
It avoids lock-in; data stays open to many tools
It forces reliance on a single vendor
expl: Open formats (Delta Lake, Parquet) avoid vendor lock-in, keeping data accessible to a range of engines and tools across the ecosystem.
src: Docs: open formats in the lakehouse

stem: What are system tables in Unity Catalog?
opts: Tables exposing operational and governance metadata
expl: The system catalog exposes system tables with operational and governance metadata (usage/billing, lineage, audit logs, query history) that can be queried with SQL.

stem: Which capability lets Databricks automatically run maintenance (OPTIMIZE/VACUUM) on managed UC tables?
expl: Predictive Optimization automatically runs maintenance such as OPTIMIZE and VACUUM on managed UC tables, deciding when and where without manual scheduling.

stem: Where in Databricks SQL does an analyst write and run SQL interactively?
expl: The SQL editor is the Databricks SQL interface for writing, running, and saving queries, selecting a warehouse, and viewing results.

stem: Which statement about workspace-to-metastore assignment in Unity Catalog is correct?
opts: A workspace can have several active metastores at once
Each workspace is assigned to exactly one metastore (for its region)
There is no relationship between a workspace and a metastore
expl: Each workspace is assigned to a single UC metastore (per region). Multiple workspaces in the same region can share one metastore.

stem: Which Unity Catalog object groups schemas (databases) under one logical container?
expl: A catalog groups schemas, which in turn group tables/views/volumes/functions - the second level of the UC three-part namespace.

stem: What is the conceptual difference between a traditional data warehouse and a data lake?
opts: A warehouse does not support SQL
A lake stores only structured data
Warehouse is schema-on-write; a lake is schema-on-read
expl: Warehouse: structured data, schema-on-write, BI-optimized. Lake: raw data of any type, schema-on-read, cheap and flexible. The lakehouse combines both.

stem: Which feature shares live data with a partner who does NOT use Databricks, without replicating it?
expl: Delta Sharing is an open protocol that shares live data without replication, including to recipients who do not use Databricks (open sharing).

stem: What role does the Databricks Assistant play for an analyst in the SQL environment?
expl: The Databricks Assistant is embedded AI that helps analysts write, explain, optimize, and debug SQL directly in the editor, speeding up query authoring.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a Unity Catalog securable object?
expl: Catalogs, schemas, tables, views, volumes, and functions are UC securables. A SQL warehouse is compute governed by workspace/compute permissions, not a UC data object.

stem: What is the key difference between a managed and an external table in Unity Catalog?
opts: Managed DROP removes data and metadata; external DROP removes only metadata
External table files are managed automatically by the metastore
External tables are read-only and can never be written
expl: For a managed table Databricks manages both data and location, so DROP removes metadata and files. For external, you control the data location, so DROP removes only the metadata.
src: Exam guide: managed vs external tables

stem: Which command shows the columns and data types of a table?
expl: DESCRIBE table (or DESCRIBE TABLE) lists columns and types. DESCRIBE HISTORY shows versions; DESCRIBE DETAIL shows physical metadata.

stem: Which command lists all tables in a schema?
expl: SHOW TABLES IN <catalog>.<schema> lists the tables. SHOW SCHEMAS and SHOW CATALOGS list the levels above.

stem: An analyst wants to document what a column means so others and Genie understand it. What should they add?
opts: A comment on the column or table
expl: Comments/descriptions on tables and columns (via COMMENT ON or Catalog Explorer) document meaning, appear in discovery, and help other users and Genie.

stem: Which feature applies searchable key-value labels to assets to help classify and discover them?
expl: Tags are key-value pairs applied to catalogs, schemas, tables, and columns to classify assets and make them easier to discover and govern.

stem: An analyst runs DROP TABLE on an external table in Unity Catalog. What happens to the data?
opts: Only the metadata is removed; files remain
Both metadata and data files are removed
The data moves to a recycle bin for 7 days
expl: For external tables, DROP TABLE removes only the catalog metadata; the underlying files remain in the external location, because you manage them.

stem: How can an analyst visually inspect a table's upstream sources and downstream consumers?
opts: Through the Lineage tab in Catalog Explorer
expl: The Lineage tab in Catalog Explorer shows upstream and downstream dependencies of tables and columns, useful for understanding provenance and impact.
src: Docs: UC lineage in Catalog Explorer

stem: Which command removes all rows from a table while keeping its structure?
expl: TRUNCATE TABLE (or DELETE FROM with no WHERE) removes all rows while preserving the table and schema. DROP would remove the whole table.

stem: An analyst needs to replace NULLs in a numeric column with 0 while cleaning data in SQL. Which function fits?
expl: COALESCE(column, 0) returns the first non-null value, replacing NULL with 0 - a common SQL data-cleaning pattern.

stem: Which command renames an existing table in the catalog?
opts: ALTER TABLE old RENAME TO new
UPDATE TABLE old SET name = new
expl: ALTER TABLE <old> RENAME TO <new> renames the table. The other forms are not valid Databricks SQL.

stem: Which command returns physical metadata of a Delta table, such as location and number of files?
expl: DESCRIBE DETAIL returns physical metadata (format, location, number of files, size). DESCRIBE lists columns; DESCRIBE HISTORY lists versions.

stem: Which is a recommended practice for sensitive data that must be governed and discovered carefully?
opts: Duplicate the table across several schemas
Make the table public to simplify access
Remove all comments and tags from the table
expl: Classifying columns/tables with tags (e.g., PII) and documenting them with comments supports governance, discovery, and applying access policies to sensitive data.

stem: For non-tabular data (e.g., images, PDFs) governed by Unity Catalog, which object does an analyst use to access the files?
expl: Volumes are UC objects that govern access to non-tabular data in object storage, letting you list and read files under the catalog's governance.

stem: Which command adds a new column to an existing Delta table?
opts: ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN new STRING
expl: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN[S] is the DDL for adding columns to an existing table; the others are invalid.

stem: Which command lists the schemas (databases) available in a catalog?
expl: SHOW SCHEMAS IN <catalog> lists the schemas in a catalog. SHOW CATALOGS lists catalogs and SHOW TABLES lists tables.

stem: To standardize text values (trim spaces, normalize case) when preparing data for analysis, which approach is best?
opts: Create an alert on the query
Use SQL functions like TRIM() and LOWER() in a view
Apply ZORDER to the text column
expl: String functions such as TRIM, LOWER, and UPPER clean and standardize text; wrapping them in a view or a silver/gold table keeps the data analysis-ready.

stem: Where does an analyst find a browsable list of catalogs, schemas, and tables they are permitted to see?
expl: Catalog Explorer is the central discovery interface: it browses catalogs, schemas, tables, columns, comments, tags, permissions, and lineage the user can access.

stem: Which statement about creating a managed table from a query is correct?
opts: CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT materializes a managed Delta table
You cannot create a table from a query
CREATE TABLE always creates an external table by default
CREATE VIEW physically materializes the data
expl: CTAS (CREATE TABLE AS SELECT) creates a managed table and materializes the query result as Delta by default. Views do not materialize data.

stem: What is the simplest way for an analyst to load a small local CSV file as a table in Databricks SQL?
opts: Use the file upload UI to create a table
Write a streaming job with Auto Loader
expl: For small, one-off files, the upload UI (Add data / Create table) lets you upload the file and create a table without writing ingestion code.
src: Docs: Create table from file upload

stem: Which SQL command loads files incrementally and idempotently, skipping files already ingested?
expl: COPY INTO loads files into a Delta table incrementally and idempotently, tracking already-processed files - a SQL option for periodic loads.

stem: Which feature continuously ingests new files arriving in object storage (S3, ADLS, GCS)?
expl: Auto Loader incrementally processes new files arriving in cloud object storage, using the cloudFiles source built on Structured Streaming.

stem: An analyst wants to consume a dataset published by a provider in the Databricks Marketplace. How is the data accessed?
opts: By recreating the tables from screenshots
Via Delta Sharing, no replication needed
By manually copying files into DBFS
By downloading a CSV over email
expl: Marketplace consumption uses Delta Sharing: the consumer accesses the live shared data from the provider, with no manual replication.

stem: Which UC object securely governs access to an external object-storage path during ingestion?
expl: External locations, backed by storage credentials, define and govern access to external object-storage paths - required to read/write external data under UC.

stem: Which command creates a Delta table from existing Parquet files without rewriting the data?
expl: CONVERT TO DELTA parquet.`/path` converts Parquet files into a Delta table in place by adding the transaction log, without rewriting the data.

stem: To ingest data from an enterprise SaaS app (e.g., Salesforce) using managed connectors, which feature is intended?
expl: Lakeflow Connect provides managed connectors for SaaS apps and databases (including CDC). Auto Loader is for files in object storage.

stem: Which SQL command appends the result of a query to an existing table?
opts: INSERT INTO t SELECT ... FROM source
expl: INSERT INTO t SELECT ... appends the query result to the table. INSERT OVERWRITE would replace existing data instead.

stem: What is the difference between batch and streaming ingestion?
opts: Batch runs periodically; streaming runs continuously
expl: Batch processes finite data at intervals (e.g., daily); streaming (including Auto Loader) processes data incrementally and continuously as it arrives.
src: Exam guide: batch vs streaming ingestion

stem: A file arrives sporadically in a container and the analyst wants to process it only when it appears. Which approach is efficient?
opts: A warehouse running 24/7 doing manual polling
A job with a file-arrival trigger
expl: A file-arrival trigger (or Auto Loader with availableNow on a schedule) processes only when new files arrive, avoiding idle continuous compute.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid way to bring data into Databricks for analysis?
opts: Uploading a file through the UI
Running VACUUM on an empty directory
expl: COPY INTO, Auto Loader, and file upload are ingestion methods. VACUUM only removes obsolete data files from an existing Delta table; it does not ingest data.

stem: Which feature lets an analyst access data exposed by another organization that also uses Databricks, without copying files?
opts: Exporting everything to CSV and re-importing
Granting access to the other company's cluster
expl: Delta Sharing Databricks-to-Databricks shares live data between organizations using UC, governed and without replication - the recommended cross-account access.

stem: Before running a query in the SQL editor, what must the analyst ensure is active?
expl: To run queries in Databricks SQL you need a running SQL warehouse selected as the query's compute.
src: Docs: run queries on a SQL warehouse

stem: Which clause filters rows BEFORE aggregation in a query with GROUP BY?
expl: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Swapping the two is a common mistake.

stem: An analyst needs only the categories whose total sales exceed 1000. Which clause enforces that on the aggregated result?
expl: HAVING applies the condition to results aggregated by GROUP BY; WHERE would act before aggregation and cannot reference the aggregate.

stem: To count distinct orders per day from (order_date, order_id), which aggregation is correct?
expl: COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) grouped by order_date counts unique orders per day. Summing the id is meaningless and COUNT(*) counts rows, not distinct values.

stem: Which JOIN returns only rows that have a match in both tables?
expl: INNER JOIN returns only rows matching in both tables on the join condition. LEFT/FULL preserve rows without a match.

stem: Which JOIN keeps all rows from the left table, filling the right columns with NULL when there is no match?
expl: A LEFT (OUTER) JOIN returns all left rows and NULLs for the right columns where there is no match.

stem: What does a CROSS JOIN produce between two tables?
expl: CROSS JOIN produces the Cartesian product: every row of the first table combined with every row of the second. Use carefully due to result size.

stem: Which construct defines named, reusable subqueries at the start of a query to improve readability?
opts: A CTE using the WITH clause
expl: A CTE (Common Table Expression), defined with WITH name AS (...), creates a named temporary result set reusable within the same query.

stem: Which set operator combines two queries' results and removes duplicates?
expl: UNION stacks results of two compatible queries and removes duplicates. UNION ALL keeps duplicates.

stem: Which operator returns only rows present in the first query but absent from the second?
expl: EXCEPT (MINUS) returns rows from the first query that do not appear in the second. INTERSECT returns rows common to both.

stem: Which clause returns only rows with unique values (removes full-row duplicates) in the result?
expl: SELECT DISTINCT removes duplicate rows based on the selected columns. GROUP BY groups for aggregation rather than simply de-duplicating.

stem: How do you return the top 10 rows after sorting by value descending?
expl: In Databricks SQL use ORDER BY value DESC followed by LIMIT 10. The TOP n syntax is not supported.

stem: Which expression implements per-row conditional logic, returning different labels based on a condition?
opts: CASE WHEN condition THEN ... ELSE ... END
expl: CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END evaluates conditions per row and returns the matching value - the standard conditional expression in SQL.

stem: Which window function numbers rows within an ordered partition?
expl: ROW_NUMBER() over a window (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...) assigns a sequential number per row in the partition - useful to pick the latest row per key.

stem: How do RANK() and DENSE_RANK() differ when there are ties?
opts: RANK cannot be used with OVER
RANK leaves gaps after ties; DENSE_RANK leaves no gaps
expl: On ties, RANK skips positions (e.g., 1,1,3) while DENSE_RANK keeps the sequence without gaps (e.g., 1,1,2).

stem: Which window function reads the value of the PREVIOUS row within an ordered partition (e.g., to compute change)?
expl: LAG() returns a prior row's value in the ordered window; LEAD() returns a following row's value - useful to compare consecutive periods.

stem: What is the best way to keep only the most recent record per key in a table with history?
opts: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY ts DESC) and filter = 1
GROUP BY key with no aggregation
expl: A window ordered by timestamp DESC with ROW_NUMBER() and a filter = 1 selects the most recent row per key. DISTINCT alone cannot control which row remains.

stem: What is a VIEW in Databricks SQL?
opts: A saved query that stores no data
A physical copy of the data
expl: A view is a named query that runs when referenced and stores no data, unlike a table, which persists data.

stem: Which command creates a temporary view visible only in the current session?
opts: CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP VIEW v AS SELECT ...
expl: CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP VIEW creates a session-scoped temporary view that disappears when the session ends. Permanent views live in the catalog.

stem: Which command creates a table that materializes the result of a query?
opts: CREATE TEMP VIEW t AS SELECT ...
expl: CTAS creates and materializes a table from the query result. Views (temporary or not) do not materialize data.

stem: How do you query a Delta table as it was at version 5 (time travel)?
opts: SELECT * FROM table VERSION AS OF 5
expl: Time travel by version uses VERSION AS OF <n>; by date uses TIMESTAMP AS OF '...'. The other syntaxes do not exist.

stem: Which command shows the version history (operation, user, timestamp) of a Delta table?
expl: DESCRIBE HISTORY lists the operation history (INSERT, MERGE, OPTIMIZE, etc.) with user and timestamp, useful for auditing and time travel.

stem: Which command upserts (updates existing and inserts new) rows from a source into a target table?
opts: MERGE INTO target USING source ON ... WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT
expl: MERGE INTO performs an upsert in a single transactional operation: it updates matching rows and inserts new ones.

stem: What does INSERT OVERWRITE do to a table?
opts: Replaces the table's contents with new data
expl: INSERT OVERWRITE replaces existing data (of the table or affected partitions) transactionally. It differs from INSERT INTO, which appends.

stem: Which function converts a string like '2024-03-01' to the date type?
expl: to_date() converts strings to the date type (with an optional format). For timestamps use to_timestamp().

stem: Which function extracts the year from a date column?
expl: year(col) returns the year. month(), day(), and EXTRACT(YEAR FROM col) are alternatives.

stem: Which function computes the number of days between two dates?
expl: datediff(end, start) returns the number of days between the two dates. date_add/date_sub add or subtract days from a date.

stem: Which expression explicitly converts a string column to an integer?
expl: CAST(col AS INT) performs the explicit type conversion. Databricks also accepts the col::INT syntax.

stem: Which function concatenates two text columns with a separator?
expl: concat_ws(separator, ...) concatenates strings with a separator; concat(...) concatenates without one.

stem: Which function extracts a substring matching a regular-expression group?
expl: regexp_extract(col, pattern, group) returns the part matching the regex group. regexp_replace substitutes matches.

stem: To turn each element of an array column into a separate row, which function do you use?
expl: explode() produces a new row for each array element (or map entry). collect_list does the opposite, aggregating values into an array.

stem: How do you access a nested field of a struct column named address with subfield city?
expl: Struct fields are accessed with dot notation: address.city. For semi-structured JSON, the colon notation (col:field) is used.

stem: Which notation navigates semi-structured JSON stored in a string/variant column?
expl: In Databricks SQL the colon notation (col:field) navigates semi-structured JSON and can chain fields and indexes.

stem: Which higher-order function applies a transformation to each array element and returns a new array?
expl: transform(array, x -> expr) applies the expression to each element and returns a new array, without needing to explode.

stem: Which aggregate function sums a column's values per group?
expl: SUM(col) sums numeric values per group. COUNT counts rows; COLLECT_LIST aggregates into an array.

stem: Given SELECT category, AVG(amount) FROM t GROUP BY category, what does the query return?
opts: The sum of amounts per row
The average amount for each category
expl: Grouping by category and applying AVG(amount) returns the average amount within each category - one row per category.

stem: What does a query parameter enable in a Databricks SQL query?
opts: Substituting values into the query dynamically
expl: Query parameters pass dynamic values (dates, categories) into the query, letting it be reused with different inputs, including in dashboards.

stem: How can an analyst have a query run automatically at defined intervals?
opts: Schedule a refresh on the query
expl: Databricks SQL can schedule a query's refresh on an interval (cron), keeping results and dashboards up to date automatically.

stem: What is an advantage of saving a query in Databricks SQL?
opts: It can be reused, scheduled, and shared
It starts storing the data physically
expl: Saved queries can be re-run, parameterized, scheduled, shared, and used as the dataset for visualizations and dashboards.

stem: Which clause sorts the result first by order_date ascending, then by amount descending?
opts: ORDER BY order_date ASC, amount DESC
ORDER BY order_date, amount DESC ASC
expl: ORDER BY accepts multiple columns with independent directions: ORDER BY order_date ASC, amount DESC.

stem: What is the purpose of a correlated subquery in a WHERE clause?
opts: To filter outer rows using per-row values
expl: A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query and is evaluated per row, enabling filters like EXISTS or row-dependent comparisons.

stem: Which function returns the maximum value of a column per group?
expl: MAX(col) returns the largest value per group in an aggregation. GREATEST compares columns on the same row and does not aggregate.

stem: Which command creates a schema (database) inside a catalog?
expl: CREATE SCHEMA <catalog>.<schema> (equivalent to CREATE DATABASE) creates the schema. CREATE CATALOG creates the level above.

stem: Which is the correct way to join two tables on a common key in SQL?
opts: FROM a JOIN b ON a.id = b.id
expl: A relational join uses FROM a JOIN b ON a.key = b.key. UNION stacks rows; MERGE is for upserts.

stem: Which clause replaces a chain of OR conditions by testing membership in a list of values?
expl: IN (...) tests whether a column matches any value in a list, equivalent to several chained ORs but more readable.

stem: Which predicate correctly filters rows with amount inclusively between 10 and 20?
expl: BETWEEN 10 AND 20 is inclusive of both bounds. The non-BETWEEN equivalent would be amount >= 10 AND amount <= 20 (AND, not OR).

stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid Databricks SQL way to limit a result to 100 rows?
opts: SELECT * FROM t QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY c) <= 100
SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY c LIMIT 100
expl: Databricks SQL uses LIMIT (and supports QUALIFY with window functions). The SQL Server-style SELECT TOP n syntax is not supported.

stem: Where does an analyst see a list of previously executed queries, with duration, status, and user?
expl: Query History shows queries run in the workspace with metrics such as duration, status, warehouse, and user - the starting point for performance analysis.

stem: Which tool details how a query executed, exposing bottlenecks like large scans and shuffles?
expl: The query profile shows the execution plan and per-operator metrics (rows read, time, bytes, shuffle), helping identify bottlenecks and optimize the query.

stem: An analyst reruns the same query twice with unchanged data and the second run is nearly instant. What explains this?
expl: Databricks SQL can serve results from cache when the query and underlying data have not changed, returning almost instantly without reprocessing.

stem: What does enabling Photon typically improve for an analyst's queries?
opts: The execution time of SQL queries
expl: Photon accelerates SQL and DataFrame workloads with a vectorized engine, reducing query time and cost on compatible workloads.

stem: Which feature automatically manages data layout to speed up filters, without manual partitioning or ZORDER?
expl: Liquid Clustering manages data layout flexibly (and lets you change clustering keys) to improve data skipping, replacing manual partitioning and ZORDER in current guidance.

stem: Which command compacts many small files in a Delta table into larger ones to improve read speed?
expl: OPTIMIZE performs bin-packing, consolidating small files into larger ones and improving read performance. VACUUM only removes obsolete files.

stem: Why does a large number of small files hurt read performance?
opts: It adds heavy per-file I/O overhead
expl: Many small files add metadata and per-file I/O overhead; compacting with OPTIMIZE (or auto compaction / Liquid Clustering) improves reads.

stem: Which SQL warehouse setting helps reduce cost when the warehouse sits idle?
opts: Increasing the minimum number of clusters
expl: Auto stop shuts down the warehouse after a period of inactivity, avoiding idle compute cost while still resuming work when needed.

stem: Increasing the t-shirt SIZE of a SQL warehouse mainly improves what?
opts: The speed of individual large queries
expl: Increasing the warehouse size gives each cluster more resources, speeding up large/complex queries. Increasing scaling (not size) is what helps with concurrency.

stem: Dashboards show many concurrent queries queuing on a warehouse. Which adjustment helps most?
opts: Shrink the cluster to the minimum size
expl: Enabling/increasing warehouse scaling adds clusters to serve more simultaneous queries, reducing queuing during concurrency peaks.

stem: Which compute option gives the fastest first-query start for ad-hoc analysis after idle time?
opts: A classic warehouse that was stopped
expl: Serverless warehouses start in seconds, so the first query after idle time runs quickly compared to provisioning a classic warehouse.

stem: Which feature keeps precomputed, incrementally refreshed results to speed up recurring aggregations and dashboards?
expl: Materialized views store a query's result and refresh it incrementally, speeding up aggregations and dashboards that repeatedly query the same data.

stem: How can an analyst examine how a table's data looked at a past point to investigate a change?
expl: Time travel lets you query earlier Delta versions by version or timestamp, useful for auditing and investigating data changes.

stem: What is a side effect of running VACUUM with default retention on time-travel capability?
opts: It has no effect on time travel
It removes old files, breaking older time-travel versions
expl: VACUUM deletes unreferenced files beyond the retention window (default 7 days), making older versions that depended on those files inaccessible.

stem: Which command reveals when and by which operation a table was modified, to correlate a data change?
expl: DESCRIBE HISTORY lists operations that changed the table (INSERT, UPDATE, MERGE, OPTIMIZE) with timestamp and user, helping correlate data changes.

stem: What is the difference between the query result cache and the warehouse disk cache?
opts: Result cache reuses a query's result; disk cache stores read data locally
expl: The result cache returns an identical repeated query's result; the disk cache keeps source data in the warehouse's local storage to speed subsequent reads, even for different queries.

stem: An analyst filters on a table's clustering/partition column. Why can this make the query faster?
opts: It skips files/partitions that cannot match
expl: Filtering on a clustering/partition column lets the engine skip files or partitions that cannot satisfy the filter (data skipping / partition pruning), reducing data read.

stem: What does data skipping rely on to avoid reading irrelevant files in a Delta table?
expl: Data skipping uses per-file statistics (such as min/max) to avoid reading files that cannot contain matching rows, reducing scanned data.

stem: The first query after starting a warehouse is slow, but subsequent ones are fast. What is the likely cause?
opts: Later runs hit the disk/result cache
expl: After the first read, data lands in the warehouse's disk cache and identical results may come from the result cache, speeding up later runs.

stem: Which feature helps identify recurring slow or expensive queries to prioritize optimization?
opts: Query history filtered by duration and cost
expl: Query history, filtered by duration, warehouse, and user, surfaces the slowest/most expensive recurring queries, guiding where to invest in optimization.

stem: What is the best way to compare performance before and after optimizing a query?
opts: Compare history/profile metrics for both runs
Look at the number of dashboards
Count how many columns the table has
expl: Comparing query history and query profile metrics (total time, bytes read, join strategy) for both runs objectively shows the optimization's effect.

stem: Why does Databricks recommend Liquid Clustering over heavy manual partitioning for new tables?
opts: It avoids skewed partitions and lets keys change
It removes the need for a warehouse
expl: Liquid Clustering avoids over-partitioning pitfalls (tiny/skewed partitions) and allows changing clustering keys flexibly without rewriting the whole table.

stem: Which capability runs OPTIMIZE and VACUUM automatically on managed tables to keep performance up without scheduling?
expl: Predictive Optimization applies maintenance (OPTIMIZE, VACUUM) automatically on managed UC tables, using ML to decide when and where.

stem: Which query profile metric helps assess how much data was actually read from storage?
expl: Scan metrics (bytes and files read) indicate data volume; high values suggest room to improve data skipping, filters, or clustering.

stem: Besides good filters, which SELECT practice reduces the amount of data a query reads?
opts: Always use SELECT * to leverage the cache
Select only the needed columns instead of SELECT *
expl: Selecting only needed columns reduces I/O and leverages the columnar format (column pruning); SELECT * reads unnecessary columns and can hurt performance.

stem: In a join between a large and a small table, which technique avoids shuffling the large table?
opts: A broadcast join of the small table
expl: A broadcast join sends the small table to every node, avoiding the costly shuffle. The engine applies this automatically when the table fits the broadcast threshold.

stem: How does filtering data as early as possible in a query help performance?
opts: It reduces the rows processed downstream
expl: Applying selective filters early reduces the number of rows flowing into joins and aggregations, lowering processing and data movement.

stem: A dashboard queries a table that receives frequent writes and now has many small files. Which action improves reads?
opts: Run OPTIMIZE to compact the files
expl: Compacting the small files with OPTIMIZE, or enabling auto compaction/optimized writes/Liquid Clustering, improves the dashboard's read performance.

stem: Which information does the query profile give to diagnose a costly join?
opts: The number of dashboards in the workspace
The join strategy and data moved between nodes
expl: The profile shows the join strategy (broadcast or shuffle) and the bytes/rows moved, helping decide whether a broadcast or better filtering would cut cost.

stem: How can an analyst analyze a table's state for a specific past day?
expl: TIMESTAMP AS OF '<date/time>' queries the table as of that point in time, within the available time-travel window.

stem: Query insights/recommendations in Databricks SQL help an analyst by doing what?
opts: Surfacing execution details and tuning suggestions
expl: Query insights expose execution details and suggestions (e.g., where time is spent), guiding the analyst toward tuning opportunities.

stem: Which is a sensible first step when a dashboard loads slowly?
expl: Inspecting the dashboard's queries in query history and the profile pinpoints which queries are slow and why, before any change is made.

stem: What does a materialized view's incremental refresh avoid compared to recomputing from scratch?
opts: Reprocessing all source data on every refresh
expl: Incremental refresh updates only what changed in the source, avoiding full recomputation each time and keeping recurring results fast.

stem: An analyst wants to keep a frequently used warehouse responsive during business hours while still controlling cost. Which balance is reasonable?
opts: Disable auto stop and use the maximum size permanently
A moderate auto-stop plus right-sized scaling
Turn the warehouse off during business hours
Set auto stop to 1 minute and a single tiny cluster
expl: A moderate auto-stop timeout keeps the warehouse warm during active periods while stopping it when idle, and scaling sized to typical concurrency balances responsiveness and cost.

stem: Which of the following does NOT improve read performance of a Delta table?
opts: Using Liquid Clustering on commonly filtered columns
Filtering on the clustering column to enable data skipping
Running OPTIMIZE to compact small files
expl: Compaction, clustering, and filtering on clustering columns improve reads. Granting SELECT only changes access control and has no effect on query performance.

stem: What is Databricks' current product for building interactive dashboards with embedded AI?
expl: AI/BI Dashboards are the current Databricks SQL dashboarding solution, with datasets, visualizations, filters, and AI features such as natural-language questions.

stem: In an AI/BI Dashboard, what defines the data that feeds the visualizations?
expl: Datasets are the SQL queries that supply data to the dashboard's visualizations and widgets; each visual references a dataset.

stem: Which visualization best shows how a metric evolves over time?
expl: A line chart shows a metric's trend along a time axis, making growth, decline, and seasonality easy to see.

stem: Which visualization is best for comparing values across discrete categories?
expl: A bar chart compares values across distinct categories side by side, the default choice for categorical comparisons.

stem: Which visualization highlights a single key number (KPI), such as total revenue this month?
expl: The counter visualization displays a single aggregated value prominently, ideal for KPIs such as total sales or user counts.

stem: Which visualization shows the relationship/correlation between two numeric variables?
expl: A scatter plot places numeric value pairs on two axes, revealing correlations, clusters, and outliers.

stem: Which visualization is appropriate for showing aggregated values by geographic region on a map?
expl: A choropleth map colors geographic regions by a metric's value, useful for spatial analysis by country/state/city.

stem: How does an analyst create a visualization from a query in Databricks SQL (classic model)?
opts: Add a visualization on the query result
expl: After running a query, the analyst adds a visualization on the result, choosing the type (bar, line, etc.) and mapping columns to axes/series.
src: Docs: create a visualization from a query

stem: What does a dashboard filter let the end user do?
expl: Filters let dashboard readers restrict the data (e.g., by date or region), interactively updating the linked visualizations.

stem: What is the purpose of a dashboard parameter?
opts: Let a reader change a value passed to the queries
expl: Dashboard parameters pass reader-chosen values (e.g., period, category) into the dataset queries, changing results dynamically and in a controlled way.

stem: What is the difference between a filter and a parameter in a dashboard?
opts: A filter creates tables; a parameter creates views
A parameter only works with streaming
A filter refines results; a parameter changes the query
expl: A filter refines what is displayed from the result; a parameter injects a value into the query (e.g., date range), changing which data is fetched.

stem: How does an analyst keep a dashboard showing recent data without refreshing manually?
expl: A refresh schedule re-runs the dashboard's queries at defined intervals, keeping the visualizations up to date automatically.

stem: What does a dashboard subscription do?
opts: Emails the dashboard on a schedule
expl: Subscriptions email a snapshot of the dashboard to recipients on a schedule, distributing results without requiring manual access.

stem: What does a Databricks SQL alert do?
opts: Notifies when a query result crosses a threshold
expl: An alert runs a query on a schedule and, when a value crosses a defined threshold, triggers notifications (email/webhook) to the configured destinations.

stem: What does an alert need in order to send notifications to a channel like email or Slack?
expl: Alerts send notifications to configured notification destinations (email, Slack, webhook, etc.), defined in the workspace settings.

stem: How does an analyst share a dashboard with a colleague who should only view it, not edit it?
opts: Grant MODIFY on the base table
expl: Dashboard sharing uses permission levels (e.g., Can View, Can Edit, Can Manage); Can View grants read-only access to the colleague.

stem: What does embedding a dashboard enable?
opts: Embedding it in an external site or app
expl: Embedding lets you place the dashboard (or a visual) into external pages and applications, bringing insights outside the Databricks UI in a controlled way.

stem: Which layout capability lets an analyst organize an AI/BI Dashboard into multiple pages/tabs?
expl: AI/BI Dashboards support multiple pages on the canvas, letting you organize visualizations by theme or audience across tabs.

stem: How can an end user export the data behind a visualization for their own analysis?
opts: Download the result (e.g., CSV) from the visualization/query
expl: Visualizations/queries let users download results (e.g., CSV/Excel) to take data into external analysis when permitted.

stem: Which visualization is useful for showing the distribution of a numeric variable across bins?
expl: A histogram groups numeric values into bins and shows the frequency in each bin, revealing the data's distribution.

stem: Which visualization is appropriate for comparing the percentage composition of a few categories in a whole?
expl: A pie chart shows each category's share of the total; it works with few slices but loses clarity with many categories.

stem: Which visualization crosses two dimensions with aggregated values in cells colored by intensity?
expl: A heatmap arranges values in a two-dimensional matrix, using color to represent intensity, useful for spotting patterns across categories.

stem: Which visualization shows data in rows and columns with totals and formatting inside the dashboard?
expl: Table and pivot visualizations display tabular data, with aggregations and formatting, useful when numeric detail matters.

stem: What is the advantage of cross-filtering in an AI/BI Dashboard?
opts: Clicking one visual filters the others on the page
expl: With cross-filtering, interacting with one visual (e.g., selecting a bar) applies the filter to the other visuals on the page, enabling connected exploration.

stem: When building a bar chart by category, which column normally goes on the X axis?
expl: In a bar chart by category, the categorical dimension goes on the X axis and the aggregated metric (e.g., sum) on the Y axis.

stem: How can an analyst aggregate data directly in a visualization (e.g., sum sales by month) without rewriting the query?
opts: Set the aggregation in the visual itself
expl: Many visualizations let you set the aggregation (sum, average, count) and grouping in the visual editor, aggregating data without changing the underlying SQL.

stem: Which practice improves a dashboard's clarity for a business audience?
opts: Clear titles, formatting, and axis labels
Using as many different colors as possible
expl: Clear titles, proper formatting (currency, percent), axis labels, and a restrained palette make a dashboard readable and trustworthy for business users.

stem: What happens when a date filter is applied at the dashboard level?
opts: It propagates the filter to the bound visuals
expl: A dashboard-level filter applies the restriction to visuals/datasets connected to the field, consistently updating the displayed results.

stem: Which feature lets a reader ask a natural-language question about the data in an AI/BI Dashboard?
expl: AI/BI features let a user ask natural-language questions about the dashboard's data, leveraging Genie to generate answers/queries.

stem: What is a benefit of a single shared dataset powering several visualizations in a dashboard?
expl: Reusing one dataset across visuals ensures they all start from the same data and reduces repeated queries, improving consistency and efficiency.

stem: For a chart combining bars and a line (e.g., revenue as bars and target as a line), which type do you use?
expl: A combo chart overlays types (bars + line), useful for comparing an absolute metric against a reference/target on the same time axis.

stem: What is the best way to ensure only authorized users see a dashboard with sensitive data?
opts: Make the dashboard public to everyone
Restrict sharing permissions and base-table access
expl: Dashboard access is controlled by its sharing permissions and the viewer's access to the underlying tables in Unity Catalog; sensitive data requires both to be restricted.

stem: What does a box plot communicate?
expl: A box plot summarizes a numeric variable's distribution (median, quartiles, and outliers), useful for comparing spread across groups.

stem: How can an analyst reuse a dashboard as a starting point for another audience without changing the original?
opts: Clone the dashboard and adjust the copy
expl: Duplicating (cloning) the dashboard creates an independent copy that can be adapted for another audience without affecting the original.

stem: What is the purpose of applying number formatting (e.g., currency, percent, decimals) to a visualization?
opts: To make values readable and clear
expl: Number formatting (currency, percent, separators, decimals) improves readability and prevents misinterpretation of the displayed values.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid Databricks SQL visualization type?
expl: Counter, heatmap, and pivot table are visualization types. A checkpoint is a Structured Streaming concept, not a visualization.

stem: When configuring an alert, what does the analyst typically define besides the query?
opts: The threshold, schedule, and notification targets
The number of columns in the table
expl: An alert is configured with the query, the triggering condition/threshold, the evaluation frequency, and the destinations that receive the notification when the condition is met.

stem: What is an AI/BI Genie space?
opts: A space for natural-language questions over curated data
expl: A Genie space lets business users ask natural-language questions about selected tables; Genie translates them to SQL and returns answers and visualizations.

stem: When creating a Genie space, which is one of the first required definitions?
opts: Selecting the tables/data the space can query
expl: Creating a Genie space starts by choosing the data scope - the tables and views it can query - defining the domain it will answer over.

stem: Why are column descriptions and table comments important for a Genie space?
opts: They help Genie generate more accurate SQL
expl: Rich metadata (comments and column descriptions) gives Genie semantic context, improving the quality and accuracy of the SQL it generates from questions.

stem: What are general instructions in a Genie space?
opts: Guidance that shapes how Genie uses the data
expl: General instructions give Genie context and rules (e.g., business definitions, conventions, default filters), improving consistency and accuracy of answers.

stem: Which capability lets the analyst provide trusted example SQL queries that Genie can reuse as reference?
expl: Providing trusted example SQL (trusted assets/example queries) teaches Genie to answer common questions correctly, serving as a reference for query patterns.
src: Docs: Genie example queries / trusted assets

stem: How can the analyst ensure Genie uses the correct logic for a specific business metric (e.g., net revenue)?
opts: Define trusted SQL expressions for the metric
expl: Trusted instructions and SQL expressions document the exact definition of business metrics, guiding Genie to apply the correct logic instead of inferring inconsistently.
src: Docs: Genie SQL expressions / certified logic

stem: What is the role of benchmark questions in a Genie space?
opts: Testing whether Genie answers key questions correctly
expl: Benchmarks are reference questions with expected answers; running them validates Genie's quality and guides adjustments to instructions and examples.

stem: When a Genie space's tables must be combined, what helps Genie join the data correctly?
opts: Describing the join relationships between tables
expl: Describing how tables relate (join keys and cardinality) improves the accuracy of queries that require combining data from multiple tables.

stem: How does an analyst share a Genie space with a business team so they can ask questions?
opts: Grant access to the Genie space
Grant MODIFY on the base table
expl: A Genie space is shared via access permissions; authorized users can ask questions, while data access still respects Unity Catalog governance.

stem: Even after a Genie space is shared, what still controls which data a user can actually query?
opts: Unity Catalog permissions on the tables
expl: Genie respects UC governance: a user only accesses data through Genie for tables they are permitted to see, preserving access control.
src: Docs: Genie and Unity Catalog permissions

stem: How can an analyst continuously maintain and improve a production Genie space?
opts: Review question history and feedback, then adjust
expl: Monitoring the questions asked, the answers, and feedback (e.g., good/bad markings) reveals gaps, allowing refinement of instructions, examples, and metadata.

stem: Which compute does Genie use to run the queries generated from questions?
opts: None; it runs locally in the browser
A SQL warehouse associated with the space
expl: Genie runs the generated SQL on a SQL warehouse associated with the space; the warehouse provides the compute for the queries.

stem: Which is an important limitation to communicate to Genie space users?
opts: It removes the need for any data governance
Answers are AI-generated and should be reviewed
expl: Being AI-based, Genie may generate incorrect SQL or misread a question; results should be reviewed and validated, especially for important decisions.

stem: Which action improves Genie's ability to answer questions about company-specific business terms?
expl: Documenting business terms, synonyms, and definitions in the space's instructions helps Genie map user language to the correct columns and metrics.

stem: What can an analyst do when they notice Genie answered a question with incorrect SQL?
opts: Fix the instructions and add a trusted example
expl: When a poor answer appears, the curator adjusts instructions and adds trusted example SQL for that pattern, improving Genie's future answers.

stem: Why does choosing a lean, well-modeled data scope improve a Genie space?
opts: It reduces ambiguity for the AI
expl: A focused scope with clean, well-described tables reduces ambiguity for Genie and raises accuracy; including too many or poorly documented tables hurts answers.

stem: What is the advantage of a Genie space for users who cannot write SQL?
opts: They get answers via natural-language questions
It builds dashboards with no data
expl: Genie democratizes data access: users without SQL can ask in natural language and get AI-generated answers, queries, and visualizations.

stem: How does Genie decide which tables and columns to use when answering a question?
opts: It randomly picks any table in the metastore
The data scope plus metadata, instructions, examples
expl: Genie relies on the space's defined data scope and on metadata, instructions, and example SQL to map the question to the correct tables and columns.

stem: Which practice increases trust in a Genie space's answers?
opts: Give unrestricted access to all tables
Validate with benchmarks and certify examples
expl: Trust comes from curation: validated benchmarks, certified examples, and continuous review make answers more consistent and reliable for users.

stem: Who is typically responsible for curating and maintaining a Genie space?
opts: The AI model on its own
expl: Curation (scope, instructions, examples, review) belongs to the author/analyst who knows the data domain; the exam places this responsibility on the analyst.

stem: What is the main difference between a Genie space and a dashboard?
opts: Genie answers ad-hoc questions; dashboards show fixed visuals
A dashboard generates AI SQL on every click
expl: A dashboard delivers curated, fixed visualizations; Genie is conversational, answering new ad-hoc natural-language questions over the space's data.

stem: When preparing data for a Genie space, why do clear, consistent column names help?
opts: They help the AI map questions to columns
expl: Descriptive, consistent column names help Genie relate a user's question to the correct columns, reducing interpretation errors.

stem: What does thumbs-up/thumbs-down feedback on Genie answers let the curator do?
opts: Spot bad answers to refine the space
expl: User feedback signals which answers were helpful or poor, guiding the curator on where to refine the space (instructions, examples, metadata).

stem: Which capability lets you verify and mark a Genie answer/query as trusted for reuse?
expl: Reviewed queries can be marked trusted/verified, serving as reference for future answers and increasing the space's consistency.

stem: Why is Genie described as part of Databricks' AI/BI strategy?
opts: Conversational AI over the same governed lakehouse data
It is a fully separate product unrelated to BI
expl: Genie and dashboards make up the AI/BI offering: both operate over governed lakehouse data, combining conversational AI exploration and curated visualizations.

stem: What happens when a user asks an ambiguous question to a well-configured Genie space?
opts: It may ask for clarification or use instructions
It grants permissions to the user
It always returns a fatal error
expl: A well-curated space uses instructions and context to interpret ambiguous questions and, when needed, Genie can ask the user to clarify.

stem: Which maintenance action is recommended when new relevant tables appear for the space's domain?
opts: Delete the space and the old data
Add the new tables to the scope with metadata
Run OPTIMIZE only on the new tables
Ignore it, since Genie discovers everything on its own
expl: Keeping the space current includes adding relevant new tables to the scope and documenting them, so Genie can answer questions about the new data.

stem: What is the benefit of pointing a Genie space at clean, modeled data (e.g., the gold layer)?
opts: More reliable answers over clean data
expl: Pointing Genie at curated (gold) data reduces inconsistency and ambiguity, producing more reliable answers than over raw or poorly modeled data.

stem: In a star schema, how are the central and surrounding tables classified?
opts: A central fact table references several dimension tables
There is no distinction of roles
Several fact tables reference one central dimension
expl: In a star schema, the fact table (metrics/events) sits at the center and links to dimension tables (descriptive context), forming a star.

stem: What does a fact table typically store?
opts: Business measures plus keys to dimensions
expl: A fact table stores quantitative measures (e.g., amount, quantity) and the foreign keys linking it to the dimensions that describe the context.

stem: What does a dimension table typically store?
opts: Descriptive attributes to filter and group facts
expl: Dimensions hold descriptive attributes (product name, category, region, calendar) used to give context to and filter/group the facts' measures.

stem: What does the grain of a fact table mean?
opts: The level of detail each row represents
The number of columns in the table
expl: The grain defines what each fact row represents (e.g., a sale, an order line, a day). Defining the grain is a fundamental step in dimensional modeling.

stem: What is the difference between normalization and denormalization in modeling?
opts: Normalization splits tables; denormalization joins to speed reads
expl: Normalization splits data into more tables to reduce redundancy; denormalization combines data (fewer joins) to speed analytical reads - a common BI trade-off.

stem: What is a surrogate key in a dimension?
opts: An artificial key used instead of the business key
expl: A surrogate key is a generated substitute key (e.g., identity/sequential) that stably identifies the dimension row, independent of changes to the business key.

stem: How does Databricks SQL automatically generate unique sequential values for a column (e.g., a surrogate key)?
opts: With an IDENTITY column (GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY)
expl: IDENTITY columns (GENERATED ALWAYS/BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY) generate sequential values automatically, useful as surrogate keys in dimensions.

stem: What is the status of primary-key and foreign-key constraints declared in Unity Catalog?
opts: They are always enforced and block invalid inserts
They only work on external tables
They do not exist in Databricks
expl: In UC, PK/FK are by default informational (not enforced): they document relationships and help BI tools and the optimizer, but do not prevent invalid data.

stem: What describes a Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) Type 2?
opts: It always overwrites the old value without keeping history
It deletes the dimension on each load
It adds a new versioned row on each change
expl: SCD Type 2 preserves history: when an attribute changes, a new versioned row is created (with validity/flag), keeping the prior state. Type 1 overwrites without history.

stem: How does the medallion architecture (bronze/silver/gold) relate to modeling for analysis?
opts: Bronze raw, silver cleaned, gold modeled for consumption
expl: The gold layer delivers modeled, aggregated data (e.g., facts and dimensions) ready for BI; silver cleans/conforms and bronze holds the raw source data.

stem: What is a reason to use a view instead of a table when modeling data for analytical consumption?
opts: To present derived data without duplicating storage
To physically store a copy of the data
To remove the need for permissions
expl: Views expose a semantic layer (renamed columns, filters, joins) over base tables without duplicating data, useful to model what the analyst consumes.

stem: Why is choosing appropriate data types (e.g., DATE/TIMESTAMP, DECIMAL) important when modeling?
opts: It ensures correct calculations and compression
It increases the number of permissions
It is irrelevant; everything can be STRING
It prevents the use of SQL
expl: Correct types enable proper operations and functions (dates, precise numeric aggregation with DECIMAL), improve compression, and avoid conversion errors in analysis.

stem: The analysts group already has USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA. To grant read on all current and future tables in schema sales, which command is correct?
opts: GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA sales TO analysts
GRANT INSERT ON SCHEMA sales TO analysts
GRANT MODIFY ON SCHEMA sales TO analysts
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA sales TO analysts
expl: GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA grants read on all tables in the schema, including future ones via inheritance. ALL PRIVILEGES is excessive and INSERT/MODIFY grant write.

stem: A user has SELECT on prod.sales.clients but cannot even reference it. What is most likely missing?
opts: USE CATALOG on prod and USE SCHEMA on sales
expl: Besides the object privilege, the user needs USE CATALOG on the catalog and USE SCHEMA on the schema to navigate to the table; without them, even referencing it fails.
src: Docs: UC USE CATALOG / USE SCHEMA

stem: Which command grants a user the ability to modify (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) data in a table?
opts: GRANT SELECT ON TABLE t TO `user@x.com`
GRANT MODIFY ON TABLE t TO `user@x.com`
expl: The MODIFY privilege grants write (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE) on the table. SELECT grants read only.

stem: Which command removes a privilege previously granted to a group?
opts: REVOKE SELECT ON SCHEMA sales FROM analysts
REMOVE SELECT ON sales TO analysts
expl: REVOKE <privilege> ON <object> FROM <principal> removes the privilege. The other syntaxes do not exist.

stem: Why is managing permissions by groups preferable to granting to individual users?
opts: A grant on the group applies to all members
Individual users cannot receive a GRANT
expl: Managing by group centralizes control: adding/removing members or granting/revoking on the group adjusts everyone's access at once, simplifying governance.

stem: How do you expose only some columns of a table to a group without giving access to the base table?
opts: Grant SELECT on a view with the allowed columns
Grant SELECT on the whole table
expl: A view can select/derive only the desired columns; you grant SELECT on the view without granting access to the base tables - a common security pattern.
src: Docs: UC views for access control

stem: Which Unity Catalog feature hides or transforms values in a sensitive column based on who queries it?
expl: Column masks apply a masking function to a column based on who runs the query, protecting sensitive data without duplicating the table.

stem: Which Unity Catalog feature dynamically restricts which ROWS a user can see in a table?
expl: Row filters apply a condition that limits returned rows based on the user/group, enabling row-level security without separate copies.

stem: Which function is used in a dynamic view to return different data based on the user's group?
expl: Dynamic views use functions like is_account_group_member() (and current_user()) to mask or filter data per user/group within the view definition.

stem: What is the best practice to ensure analysts do not accidentally change production data?
opts: Grant analysts SELECT only; reserve MODIFY
expl: Apply least privilege: analysts get SELECT only; write (MODIFY) stays with engineering roles, preventing accidental changes to production.

stem: Which command lists the current permissions on a table?
expl: SHOW GRANTS ON <object> lists the privileges granted and to whom, useful for auditing who has access.

stem: Which statement about object ownership in Unity Catalog is correct?
opts: The owner has full control over the object
Only the account admin can read any table
expl: Every securable object has an owner with full control who can grant/revoke privileges; ownership can be transferred with ALTER ... OWNER TO.

stem: Which privilege lets a user discover the existence/structure of objects without granting read access to the data?
expl: BROWSE lets users discover metadata (existence/structure) without read access to the data; SELECT already reads the data.

stem: How does privilege inheritance work in Unity Catalog?
opts: A higher-level grant is inherited by objects below
Each table always requires an individual GRANT
expl: Privileges propagate down the hierarchy: a GRANT at the catalog applies to its schemas and tables, including ones created later, simplifying management.

stem: What is the recommended way to give read access to sensitive data for several team members?
opts: Grant individually and repeat manually for each person
Create a group, add the people, and grant SELECT to the group
Use ALL PRIVILEGES on the metastore for everyone
expl: Granting to the group is recommended: access is managed in one place and member changes adjust access automatically.

stem: To automate a production dashboard/alert without depending on a personal user, which identity is recommended?
expl: Service principals are stable non-human identities, ideal for automation: they avoid dependence on personal accounts (which can be deactivated) and improve security.

stem: Which command transfers ownership of a table to another principal (e.g., a group)?
expl: ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO <principal> transfers object ownership; the new owner gains full control over it.
